$comment: Desk grade (not hands-on). Steam review quotes from the English review JSON (filter=all, 4 pages, 243 unique reviews sampled, 60% up); review ids given.
game: Legends of IdleOn (IdleOn - The Incremental MMO)
build: Steam app 1476970 as of 2026-10-15 (World 7 era; latest Steam news 2026-09-19 'JELLY OPERATOR [new content]')

package.basis: desk: Steam store data and review API (21,851 English reviews, 76% positive, Mostly Positive), idleon.wiki AFK and Gem Shop pages, a vaporlens review aggregate and prior repo research; not played.

fun.source: desk estimate: below Melvor (65.4, eval/calibration/melvor-idle.scorecard.json) because reviews describe overload, chores and FOMO; well above the mediocre idle RPG composite (30.8) because of parallel characters and a steady stream of new systems

evidence.quote: the game is praised for its creativity, art style
too bad the characters look like ... and arent cute
described as a 2D pixel-art idle MMORPG

dims.note: Coherent cartoon-pixel MMO look, crowded late screens; competent, mildly distinctive.

evidence.quote: no video controls whatsoever. its just a mobile game.
IdleOn (light MapleStory-like loops)

dims.note: Little review comment on animation; inferred from genre and anchor. Low confidence.

evidence.quote: HUD is confusing and the controls are janky.
without wiki its easy to soft lock some areas of progression
the user interface has readability problems

dims.note: Matches the rubric's ~20 anchor: many currencies and screens, wiki needed (review 236412314: 'do not go into this game blind').

evidence.quote: English, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese — 'languages with full audio support'
only 2 of 243 sampled reviews mention music or sound at all

dims.note: Not listened. Silence in reviews suggests unremarkable audio; below the rubric's 50 anchor only by inference.

evidence.quote: 20% - Basic AFK gains (every Character)
It starts off slow with no minigames, but more mechanics and hard decisions on where to focus your effort unlock quickly.
Piles on way too many mechanics way too early on.

dims.note: AFK fighting from minute one and a second character at level 10 (idleon.wiki/wiki/Character_Creation via prior research); then a flood of systems.

evidence.quote: the game throws another system at me and I immediately get addicted all over again
an ever-growing pile of systems that demand your attention
5 Years of IdleOn Content Updates!

dims.note: New worlds and systems keep arriving for months; cost is accumulating daily chores. No ending.

evidence.quote: Create 11 unique Classes ... optimizing skill-tree builds, min-maxing your stats
hard decisions on where to focus your effort

dims.note: 11-character account with roles, skill trees, many interlocking systems; guides publish priority orders, so some choices collapse to a known best.

evidence.quote: Time candy gives you instant AFK progress on a single character!
Auto Loot Pack: 900 gems for $4.99, includes 'Auto-Loot Toggle'
a 'chance draw' from a paid currency. Guaranteed after 60 attempts ... around $250

dims.note: AFK at a 20% base rate, gem-bought time skips (Time Candy, Sand of Time, Stamina Battery) and paid auto-loot. Below the rubric's 50 anchor: the gem time skips trip the kill criterion.

evidence.quote: It's incredibly satisfying watching your account slowly turn into an absolute monster.
A lot of what would be considered repetitive ends up being very satisfying.

dims.note: Satisfaction quoted is mostly progression, not moment-to-moment feedback; low confidence.

evidence.quote: The 'white screen' problem has never been addressed for years
updates have bugs that delete progress, crash the game
freezing, stuttering, and frame rate drops

dims.note: Frequent content patches with recurring bugs; progress-loss reports exist (not counted as a session kill on desk evidence).

evidence.quote: The amount of content is insane
immense amount of content
11 unique Classes ... level 20 unique skills like Farming, Sailing, and Construction

dims.note: Matches Melvor/NGU at the 80 benchmark; seven worlds. Lapse: late-game complexity rather than shortage.

evidence.quote: The power fantasy of an MMO, with the automation of an incremental game
The incremental idle MMO where your heroes keep fighting while you're gone!

dims.note: Idle MMO with an 11-character family is a pitch few others own; screenshot reads as a generic 2D MMO.

evidence.quote: Windows only on Steam; 6 languages
I started on mobile and was able to link my progress to steam.
the user interface has readability problems

dims.note: PC + mobile with linked progress; always online; no evidence of text scaling or motion settings.

learn.practice: Parallelism as the first idle lever: a second hero early (IdleOn's second character at level 10) doubles what runs while away and gives a new decision.
learn.evidence: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1476970 — 'IdleOn lets you create 11 characters, so you'll have one of each class - each one plays a unique role in your account!'

learn.practice: Unlock systems on a steady drip so each return brings a new mechanic, but cap the chores each one adds.
learn.evidence: https://store.steampowered.com/appreviews/1476970 (review 236244523) — 'the game throws another system at me and I immediately get addicted all over again'

learn.practice: The return loop: come back, spend what was earned away, buy more upgrades, send again.
learn.evidence: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1476970 — 'Load up IdleOn the next day, spend your AFK gains earned while you were away, and buy MORE upgrades!'

learn.practice: Anti-pattern: never sell time skips or automation toggles; IdleOn's Time Candy and $4.99 auto-loot are its most resented choices.
learn.evidence: https://idleon.wiki/wiki/Gem_Shop — 'Time candy gives you instant AFK progress on a single character!'
